experiment: per-sector ZC wave vs amp -- load-angle vs geometry test
finding: PROVISIONAL: the per-sector wave tracks load angle (slides + flattens with amp), not fixed geometry. Single freq / 4 amps / open loop / one board -- pending a larger (Hz, amp) sweep.

config.loop: open (fixed uniform commutation -- cannot desync; the clean load-angle probe)
config.measure: ungated python linfit_zc_pct on valley-sampled float-minus-driven-pair-neutral; |slope|>=15 filter (drop flat/unobservable windows); [-100,200]% sanity bound

units: linfit ZC, % of the 60-degree float window, per physical sector 0..5
signatures: SLIDE: sectors move in opposite directions as amp rises (s0 4->33, s5 -57->26 climb; s2 83->17 falls); peak walks s2->s1, trough s5->s4. Fixed geometry would scale, not slide.
FLATTEN: peak-to-trough spread collapses 140->26 over 13->19%; at 19% all sectors sit at +17..+43% (near window centre, in-window).
